about.title: Personal Injury Help in Cloverdale, California
about.longDescription: Cloverdale is a small city, but its streets carry a steady flow of local and pass-through traffic. Public records show 13 injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, leaving 18 people hurt. Corridors like S Cloverdale Boulevard, N Cloverdale Boulevard, Cloverdale Boulevard, and the stretch of US-101 Southbound running through town account for a meaningful share of reported crashes. These numbers are neutral counts, not judgments about any particular road — they simply reflect how much this small city's transportation network gets used every day. If you were injured in a collision on one of these roads, or anywhere else in Cloverdale, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, we don't charge you anything, and any attorney you're connected with typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Our job is simply to make that first connection easier so you can focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover at all.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate it.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Lost
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life, so your claim isn't artificially boxed in.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, which means they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no bill just for having a conversation.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys. We don't provide legal advice or represent you directly — the attorney you're connected with handles your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim in California. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city or county road issue, the deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's wise to act promptly.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Cloverdale?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along S Cloverdale Boulevard, N Cloverdale Boulevard, Cloverdale Boulevard, and the local stretch of US-101 Southbound, with reports also tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply neutral, publicly reported counts and not a judgment about any specific road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is just reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No, connecting through LawProactive is completely free. Attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you win or settle your case.
